items.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
items.summary: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future $e^+e^-$ colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes $e^+ e^- \to t\bar{t},\ e^+e^-\to μ^+μ^-$ and Bhabha scattering $e^+e^-\to e^+e^-$, representing the mass threshold behavior, the $Z$ pole resonance and the $s/t$-channel interplay.

items.title: Nambu’s Dynamics, Strings, and Gravitized Quantum Theory
items.summary: In this article, we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory.

items.title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
items.summary: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction. While quantum reservoir computing has been widely explored for this setting, variational quantum models tailored to sequential data remain comparatively understudied, largely because they are difficult to train.

items.title: Body in memory: the role of bodily self-consciousness in episodic memory and autonoetic consciousness
items.summary: Episodic memory (EM) enables the conscious recollection of personally experienced events, including contextual features such as visual, auditory and emotional details. However, the role of bodily signals has been largely neglected in EM, although the observer's body provides a rich bodily context during the encoding, storage and recall of events, and has recently been associated with a bodily form of self-consciousness (bodily self-consciousness; BSC).

items.summary: Abstract The entropic brain hypothesis (EBH) and irruption theory (IT) are two recent frameworks to investigate consciousness by examining neural entropy. While they differ in their theoretical commitments, both aim to advance neuroscientific investigations of consciousness without succumbing to the intelligibility problem: the impossibility for scientific inquiries to provide intelligible access to subjective experience.

items.title: 100 ± Δ t years of quantum uncertainty: From origins to modern insights
items.summary: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, marking a decisive departure from classical physics. Conceived almost a century ago through a thought experiment showing that measuring an electron's position inevitably disturbs its momentum, it began as a deceptively simple idea that sparked countless studies and grew into the rich research field it is today.

items.title: Separations Between Randomized and Exact Quantum Query Complexity for Boolean Functions
items.summary: We construct a family of total Boolean functions $F_{\mathrm{tot}}$ whose randomized and exact quantum query complexities satisfy $R(F_{\mathrm{tot}}) \ge Q_E(F_{\mathrm{tot}})^{2-o(1)}$. items.title: Randomized routing: ruling out classical networks without trusting source independence
items.summary: Network nonlocality without inputs assumes that the sources are independent, but no data can test this, since one classical source feeding all parties reproduces any correlation. Here we propose a randomized routing strategy: a source is duplicated, and the two parties it connects choose at random which copy to read.

This paper argues that the gap is not a physical problem and admits no physical solution.

items.summary: Abstract This paper examines whether comprehensive knowledge acquisition attenuates emotional experience through a thought experiment that uses large language models (LLMs). We propose that LLMs, which possess extensive propositional knowledge yet lack phenomenal consciousness, serve as philosophical instruments for isolating the knowledge variable from other cognitive attributes.

items.summary: For every finite level of the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy, we construct correlations that satisfy all its constraints but violate information causality. At each fixed level, one use of a binary-outcome correlation and one classical bit suffice for a violation that grows without bound as the number of measurement settings increases.

items.title: TCBP-JOBS: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Error Correction Decoding and Noise Learning with Near-Optimal Accuracy
items.summary: Achieving near-optimal quantum error correction (QEC) decoding accuracy often requires computationally expensive searches that limit both large-scale simulation and real-time operation. We introduce trajectory-calibrated belief propagation (TCBP), which learns calibrated fault probabilities from BP trajectories, and jittered OSD beam search (JOBS), which uses these probabilities to guide parallel GPU searches.

items.title: Generalized Rotating-Wave Approximations Hierarchy for the Interacting Two-Qubit Rabi Model
items.summary: We investigate the two-qubit quantum Rabi model for identical qubits symmetrically coupled to a single bosonic mode and interacting with each other through transverse and longitudinal couplings. We extend the adiabatic, generalized rotating-wave (GRWA), and squeezed generalized rotating-wave (SGRWA) approximations to include the qubit-qubit interactions, including self-consistent and variational choices of the bosonic parameters.

items.title: Measurement-informed dynamical decoupling for fidelity preservation on large-scale quantum processors
items.summary: Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a key technique for suppressing decoherence and preserving the performance of quantum algorithms. We introduce a measurement-based DD (MDD) protocol that determines control unitary gates from partial measurements of noisy subsystems, with measurement overhead scaling linearly with the number of subsystems.

items.title: Liquid Integrated Network as Candidate Substrate for Artificial Consciousness
items.summary: Whether artificial intelligence (AI) system allows for generating machine consciousness has been a “grand challenge” which however must be answered in this day and age. Most contemporary AI is implemented on large scale solid-state electronic hardware, whereas biological consciousness is supported by much smaller sized space within a fluid-rich brain.

items.title: Digital engineering for quantum communication networks: A systematic review of models, simulators, and testbeds

As these systems become more complex, there is increasing interest in digital methods that can support analysis, prediction, and performance assessment without relying exclusively on physical experimentation.

Existing quantum debugging approaches primarily target logical-level circuits and do not naturally support debugging within realistic FTQC execution flows.

items.title: Almost-quantum correlations violate information causality
items.summary: Abstract Information causality (IC), a generalization of the no-signalling principle, states that communicating m classical bits cannot give the receiver access to more than m bits of information about the sender's independent data. Although IC holds in quantum theory and excludes a broad class of supra-quantum correlations, its validity for the almost-quantum set has remained open.

items.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
items.summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions.

items.title: Physical predictions in closed quantum gravity

This raises a basic puzzle: how can a unique quantum-gravity state give rise to semiclassical physics, measurement outcomes, and classical probabilities?

items.title: Quantum Symmetry and Entanglement Horizons: Theory, Photonic Systems, and Quantum Inspired Data Analytics
items.summary: This book examines the role of translational symmetry in shaping and stabilising quantum entanglement across spatial and temporal domains. Building on foundational concepts from the EPR paradox and Bell’s theorem, it introduces a nodal–antinodal framework to explain coherence preservation and entanglement amplification.

items.title: Qualiaphobic artificial neural networks (and why to build them)
items.summary: This paper introduces qualiaphobic AI: artificial neural network architectures that are hostile to theories of consciousness. I show that qualiaphobia can be well-justified by knowledge about theories of consciousness, like when such theories are trivial or unfalsifiable or contradicted by overwhelming scientific evidence.

items.summary: Quantum machine learning (QML) has emerged as a rapidly developing field at the intersection of quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and data science. items.title: Practical limitations on robustness and scalability of quantum Internet
items.summary: Abstract The realization of a desirably functional quantum Internet is hindered by fundamental and practical challenges such as high loss during transmission of quantum systems, decoherence due to interaction with the environment, and fragility of quantum states under measurement. We study the implications of these constraints by analyzing the limitations on the scaling and robustness of the quantum Internet.

items.title: Common phenomenal and neural substrate geometry in visual motion perception
items.summary: What is a possible physical substrate of the qualitative aspects of consciousness (qualia)? Answering this question is a central goal of consciousness research. items.summary: We study single-electron scattering in a tight-binding chain capacitively coupled to double quantum dots, which act as dynamical two-level-system impurities with electrically tunable level splittings. items.title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
items.summary: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) requires suppressing errors in both space and time, yet standard logical memory experiments primarily probe spatial faults. Here, we use a 105-qubit Willow superconducting quantum processor to realize and scale the surface code stability experiment, which is alternatively sensitive to temporal error chains.

items.title: Peak state transfer in trees and the cost of distance
items.summary: There is peak state transfer between vertices $u$ and $v$ in a graph $G$ if there exists a time $t$ for which $|(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm i t M})_{u,v}|$ saturates the triangle inequality imposed by its spectral decomposition and $M$ is either the adjacency or Laplacian matrix. We show that peak state transfer at distance $d$ requires $\frac{d^3}{24}(1 + o(1))$ edges in the adjacency case, $Ω(d^2)$ edges in the Laplacian case, and that the leading coefficient in the former is tight.

items.title: Optimal Quantum Sensing Algorithms for Discrete-Frequency Spectroscopy
items.summary: Spectroscopy is a versatile tool that drives scientific discovery and underpins modern technologies. Quantum sensing offers promising opportunities to advance spectroscopy through enhanced sensitivity and spectral and spatial resolution.

items.title: The speed limit of gravitational entanglement and the cost of noise
items.summary: Is gravity quantum? A proposed test lets two small masses, each in a superposition of two places, become entangled through their mutual gravity. Gravity is weak, so the masses must stay coherent for seconds while random forces disturb them.

items.title: Exponential Quantum Memory Advantage for Late-Graph Smoothness and Spectral Estimation
items.summary: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. Memory becomes the bottleneck when the neighbour graph arrives only after data erasure, a late-graph setting motivated by dispersed sensor networks and telemetry.

items.title: Entanglement distillation, nonlocal magic, and state sharing in an isospectral non-Hermitian bipartite model
items.summary: An invertible nonunitary similarity deformation leaves a two-qubit Hamiltonian's spectrum unchanged while varying a selected normalized right eigenstate in the fixed physical inner product. We embed this state in a two-parameter maximally correlated family that includes local dephasing and noisy circuit preparation.

items.title: Quantum Networks with Realistic Photonic Memories
items.summary: Ensemble based photonic memories paired with photon pair sources are the essential ingredient for many quantum networking protocols. Most protocols and theoretical analyses focus on networks of identical nodes, however, realistic networks consist of nodes that may vary from device to device.

items.title: Experimental simulation of a Hilbert-space inner-product change
items.summary: We simulate an effective change in a single qubit's inner product (IP) by implementing the channel $\mathcal{F}^η$ on a superconducting quantum processor. Whereas previous experiments simulated parity-time (PT)-symmetric dynamics with a fixed IP, this experiment implements the IP-change channel itself for metrics associated with PT-symmetric systems.

items.title: Plenitude of ideal correlations explains quantum theory
items.summary: We show that the Hilbert-space formalism and the Born rule of quantum theory are singled out by the following principle: every correlation that is possible in a theory in which every observable admits an ideal measurement is physically realizable. An ideal measurement is one that yields the same outcome when repeated and does not disturb any compatible observable.

items.title: Localization transition in a spin chain with an exact Fock-space tree
items.summary: Many-body localization is often pictured as Anderson localization on the graph of many-body configurations. Strongly correlated disorder and a dense net of loops, however, make this graph hard to analyze.

items.title: Geometry of squeezed states. The phase-space metric, relative vacua and cosmology
items.summary: Geometry enters quantum theory in two places. The space of quantum states carries a symplectic form, which generates unitary evolution, and a metric, which governs uncertainties and transition probabilities.

items.title: Rethinking Entropic Uncertainty: How measuring without a trace leads to longer keys
items.summary: In recent years, the entropic uncertainty relation (EUR) has been one of the most prominent tools to obtain tight key rates secure against general coherent attacks for a broad class of quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. Despite its success, the fundamental question of how to incorporate the statistics of more than two mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) directly into the EUR is yet to be answered.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning designs Quantum Repeater Protocols on Networks beyond the Chain Scenario
items.summary: Small-scale quantum repeater protocols have been shown to distribute entanglement over existing telecommunication infrastructure by means of short range quantum communications and long range classical messages. For larger networks, there are a number of theoretical proposals about how to operate the network to achieve a good performance under varying metrics.

items.title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
items.summary: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(π/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\fracπ{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $π/2$ and $π/4$, respectively.

items.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
items.summary: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields.

items.title: Vanishing Relative Distance of Uniformly Random CSS LDPC Codes Built from Permutation Matrices
items.summary: Classical random regular low-density parity-check codes can have minimum distance growing linearly with block length. We study CSS check matrices formed as full $J\times L$ arrays of arbitrary $P\times P$ permutation matrices, sampled uniformly subject to commutation.

items.title: Sequential strategy for depolarizing strength estimation
items.summary: We study the advantages of applying a sequential strategy for enhancing the precision in estimating the strength $p$ of a depolarizing channel, using qudit and two-qubit probes. The sequential strategy requires that the same depolarizing channel is repeatedly applied $M$ times to the quantum probe.

items.title: Catalytic compression of classical communication in exact entanglement transformations
items.summary: Entanglement catalysis is usually associated with making otherwise impossible transformations possible. Here we show that it can also change how much classical communication a transformation requires.

items.title: Quantum adiabatic and diabatic optimization: A Hilbert space engineering strategy with Rydberg arrays
items.summary: Neutral-atom arrays provide a versatile platform for encoding combinatorial optimization problems with arbitrary graph connectivity [Nguyen et al., PRX Quantum 4, 010316 (2023)]. Although the dynamics of individual encoding gadgets has been studied [Bombieri et al., PRX Quantum 6, 020306 (2025)], understanding annealing bottlenecks in larger networks remains challenging.

items.title: Experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity in discrete time crystals
items.summary: Discrete time crystals (DTCs) are almost always analyzed under the Born-Markov approximation, in which the environment is memoryless. We show that a reservoir with a finite correlation time $τ_m$ leaves an exact and strikingly simple imprint on the stroboscopic dynamics of DTCs, which can be used as an experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity.

items.title: SCOPE: A Physical Execution Latency-Guided Quantum Circuit Compilation Framework
items.summary: Quantum computing requires compilers to translate algorithms represented in the quantum circuit model into unitary operations supported by physical devices. Limited coherence time makes physical execution latency an important compilation objective.

items.title: Quantum-Assisted D-FACTS Scheduling for Moving Target Defense under Switching Limits
items.summary: Moving target defense with distributed flexible alternating-current transmission system (D-FACTS) devices re- quires activation decisions as operating points change. Switching limits couple these decisions, but period-by-period rankings can overlook combinations needed to complete low-activation schedules.

items.title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
items.summary: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability.

items.title: What kind of quantum advantage is this?
items.summary: Quantum advantage encompasses fundamentally different claims, from resource reductions to exponential separations in sample complexity. Evaluating these claims requires distinguishing how an algorithm achieves an advantage from what is necessary for the separation and how strongly it is supported against classical alternatives.

items.title: Specifying & Verifying Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
items.summary: Building quantum computers is challenging due to the noise that affects qubits. Quantum error correction tackles noise by encoding information in quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes.

items.title: Interaction Landscapes of Structurally Distorted Toroidal Classical Spin Textures
items.summary: We develop a classical discrete magnetostatic model of localized magnetic moments arranged in a toroidal texture, where the moments are represented by static current loops and study the behavior of the magnetic dipole-dipole interaction under several types of structural deformations. The purpose is to disentangle effects due to geometric and magnetic deformations, including elliptical, lopsided, alternating, and tilted configurations.

items.title: No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in dimension ten contains the Fourier pair or three product bases
items.summary: With computer-assisted proofs that $\mathbb{C}^6$ admits at most three mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) now available, $\mathbb{C}^{10}$ is the smallest dimension in which it is unknown whether a complete set of $d+1=11$ MUBs exists; only three MUBs are known. We prove that every triple of mutually unbiased product bases of $\mathbb{C}^2\otimes\mathbb{C}^5$ is strongly unextendible: no vector is unbiased to all three bases.

items.title: Observation of Crossover from Repulsive to Attractive Interactions between Two $nS$-Rydberg Atoms in Dual-Species Atom Arrays
items.summary: Dual-species Rydberg atom arrays provide a flexible platform for engineering long-range interactions beyond the conventional isotropic blockade regime. We spectroscopically study interactions between different $s$-state Rydberg levels in a $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$--$^{85}\mathrm{Rb}$ optical-tweezer array.

items.title: Deterministic nonlinear domain engineering algorithm with variable sub-coherence-length domains
items.summary: We present a new and improved deterministic algorithm that calculates the poling domains for the implementation of arbitrary phase-matching functions (PMF) in quasi-phase-matched nonlinear crystals for parametric down-conversion photon sources. In contrast to previous work, the algorithm presented here makes full use of the limits of the fabrication process, such as the minimum feature size and resolution of the lithographic process underpinning the poling procedure.

items.title: Stabilizer-Restricted Antidistinguishability in Quantum Computation with Magic States
items.summary: An antidistinguishing measurement for a family of preparations excludes at least one preparation for every possible outcome, constraining 'classical' representations of these processes, known as ontological models. We develop this connection within quantum computing with magic states (QCM), a universal model of quantum computation.

items.title: Reversal of dynamical backaction and cooling below the quantum backaction limit in Floquet-driven multimode optomechanical resonators
items.summary: Dynamical backaction describes how a driven cavity field responds with delay to mechanical motion, and can be used to cool that motion toward its quantum ground state or amplify it into self-oscillation. Control over this interaction underpins laser cooling, high-fidelity state preparation, quantum transduction, and phonon lasing.

items.title: Closing the loop on memory: accurate, shallow and transferable decoding of quantum LDPC codes
items.summary: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have attracted interest for fault-tolerant quantum computing because their high-rate constructions offer a route to reduced qubit overhead. Realizing this potential requires reliable decoding.

items.title: Subwavelength confinement of optical and acoustic waves for enhancing Brillouin gain in a planar waveguide structure
items.summary: We propose a planar waveguide structure consisting of two layers separated by a gap that provides subwavelength confinement of optical and acoustic modes and a large overlap integral between them. This, in turn, leads to an increase in Brillouin gain.

items.title: Success Probability of Block-Encoding Methods
items.summary: Block-encoding methods apply nonunitary functions $f(\widetilde H)$ of a normalized Hermitian operator on a quantum computer, but only upon a successful postselection, which introduces a shot overhead rarely included in resource estimates. We analyze the success probability $p^{(f)}_{\mathrm{success}}=\sum_n w_n|f(\tilde E_n)|^2$ of three constructions, namely linear combination of unitaries (LCU), qubitization and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT), where $w_n$ are the weights of the input state on the…

items.title: Relaxing the i.i.d. state preparation assumption with the block QKD protocol
items.summary: In this work, we propose a novel approach to handling the independent and identically distributed assumption for the state preparation in prepare-and measure QKD protocols. Contrary to previous approaches, we do not prove the security using sub-protocols, and instead opt to guarantee security in the presence of correlations by dividing the communication into finite blocks of consecutive pulses, and adding an additional assumption of no dependence between each block.

items.title: How many events does entanglement-based positronium imaging need? Information limits of Compton polarimetry with CZT detectors
items.summary: The degree of polarisation correlation of the two annihilation photons, measured by Compton polarimetry, has been proposed as a PET biomarker of tissue microstructure, but the statistics it requires have not been quantified. We parameterise the measurement by the linear-polarisation correlation coefficient $κ$ ($κ=1$ maximally entangled, $1/2$ separable), derive the classical Fisher information of double-Compton events and compare it with the quantum Fisher information, relate $κ$ to the annihilation channels of…

items.title: Global bound-state spectrum and spin- and angular-momentum-dependent confinement in an inverse-$3/2$ magnetic quantum dot
items.summary: We investigate the bound-state spectrum and confinement thresholds of a two-dimensional electron governed by the Schrödinger--Pauli equation in an inverse-$3/2$ radial magnetic-field profile. The radial problem reduces to the biconfluent Heun equation, but instead of restricting the solution to the quasi-exact polynomial sector, we impose the bound-state condition globally through a spectral Wronskian between the endpoint-selected Frobenius solution and the subdominant asymptotic solution.

items.title: Static Bounds on Thermal Fast Scrambling
items.summary: Scrambling, the process by which initially localized quantum information spreads across an interacting many-body system, is a hallmark of quantum chaos and plays a central role in understanding black hole dynamics. In thermal systems, the chaos bound of Maldacena, Shenker and Stanford limits the exponential growth rate of out-of-time-order correlations to $2π/β$, assuming that time-ordered correlation functions factorize after a dissipation time.

items.title: Metrological Channels Induced by Encrypted Quantum Cloning: Optimal-Probe Fisher-Information Broadcasting and Single-Use Operational Recovery
items.summary: Encrypted quantum cloning creates multiple individually inaccessible signal systems from which an unknown input state can be recovered by combining any selected signal with a shared quantum key. Here we study parameter estimation when a local sensing transformation is applied after encrypted cloning and before decryption.

items.title: Variational Corrections to Strong-Disorder Renormalization in the Two-Dimensional Random Transverse Field Ising Model on Quantum Hardware
items.summary: Strong-disorder renormalization-group (SDRG) methods provide an effective description of disordered quantum many-body systems by identifying the dominant couplings for the low energy physics. However, the resulting renormalization-group flow is approximate and neglects correlations beyond the RG description.

items.title: Efficient $XX$ Placement Strategies for Energy-Gap Enhancement in Quantum Annealing
items.summary: Quantum annealing offers the prospect of a computational advantage over classical methods for certain classes of combinatorial optimisation problems. Its performance, however, is fundamentally constrained by the minimum spectral gap between the ground state and the first excited state encountered during the annealing process.

items.title: Non-Hermitian edge accretion
items.summary: Under the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE), it is generally taken for granted that the open boundary condition (OBC) spectrum is encircled by the periodic boundary condition (PBC) spectrum. Intuitively, this is because boundaries tend to block the directed NHSE amplification, thereby suppressing $\operatorname{Im}(E)$.

items.title: A simple solvable $Z_N$ Hamiltonian in any dimension
items.summary: We construct local $Z_N$ clock Hamiltonians from Baxter-Fendley chains coupled according to an arbitrary finite oriented simple transverse graph. Bounded edge lengths and vertex degrees give finite-range multispin interactions, with $2d$-site bulk terms on a $d$-dimensional rectangular lattice.

items.title: Genuine multipartite entanglement in ring-shaped Hubbard models
items.summary: Spin states can be extracted from many-electron systems by detecting electrons at a set of lattice sites, which act as particle labels. Here we quantify the genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) of such spin states, which are generally mixed, in standard and extended Hubbard rings, together with the corresponding detection probability.

items.title: Near-synchronous multiphoton quantum interference
items.summary: Nonclassical multiphoton interference is an important resource for optical quantum information processing, and its output statistics depend on the distinguishability of the input photons. In this paper, using time delay as a tunable parameter, we theoretically analyze the interference behavior of independent pure-state single photons with identical Gaussian spectral envelopes under near-synchronous conditions.

items.title: Observable Spectral Framework for Noisy Amplitude Amplification: Stopping Stability and Correction
items.summary: Stopping rules for noisy amplitude amplification often rely on channel-specific success-probability formulas, limiting their transfer across noise mechanisms. We develop an observable spectral framework for stationary noisy standard amplitude amplification under explicit leading-mode, spectral-separation, and residual-control conditions.

items.title: Noise-Aware Testing of NISQ Quantum Programs: Self-Baseline Oracle with a Controlled False-Positive Rate
items.summary: Testing quantum programs on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices faces a test-oracle problem: hardware noise and finite-shot sampling make the runs of a correct program vary as much as those of a faulty one, so oracles with a fixed acceptance threshold produce false positives that depend on the program and the backend. We present a noise-aware testing framework built on self-baseline calibration: each run of the program under test is compared with repeated executions of a trusted reference program on…

items.title: Quantum Sensor of Mechanical Vibrations
items.summary: We report the use of a single trapped-ion motional mode as a probe of mechanical vibrations of the Paul trap structure. By exciting vibrations of the trap using an ultrasonic transducer mounted outside the vacuum chamber and probing the ion motion through motional sideband interactions, we observe a clear resonance response of the axial mode.

items.title: Relaxation Critical Dynamics of Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
items.summary: Strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) is unique to mixed states: strong symmetry is broken while weak symmetry is preserved, requiring two order parameters. We study the critical relaxation of both order parameters in a monitored $\mathbb{Z}_2$ circuit, which maps exactly onto two nested bond-percolation problems.

items.title: Postselection on Halting and Reductions to the Halting Problem
items.summary: A probabilistic Turing machine is an ordinary Turing machine that may also toss fair coins, with no limit on its running time or memory. If it always halts, it decides only computable problems.

items.title: Lieb-Robinson Bounds for Electric Quantum Walks
items.summary: We derive Lieb-Robinson type bounds with optimal propagation velocity for shift-coin and split-step quantum walks in rational electric fields. The velocity decays exponentially fast in the period of the field, showing long intervals of suppressed spreading.

items.title: Quantum Sensing of Defects
items.summary: Metrology of defects (or impurities) is a major challenge in quantum sensing, with implications for material science, nano-scale metrology, and the development of high-precision quantum devices. In this work, we employ single and multi excitation sensors for the metrology of defects, with the system Hamiltonian encoding the structure of the sensor and the defect treated as a perturbation potential.

items.title: Quantum geometric spectroscopy with Schrödinger cat states
items.summary: We propose a spectroscopic approach that reads out the quantum geometry of matter from the quantum decoherence of Schrödinger-cat light, in the same way that optical absorption reads out the energy structure of matter. For a cat-state probe comprising a superposition of two coherent states, the interbranch coherence of the outgoing light encodes the overlap between the matter states driven by the two branches.

items.title: Rate-1/2 Quantum LDPC Codes for Multi-tier Superconducting Hardware
items.summary: Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, while its resource overhead is governed in large part by the encoding rate, namely the number of logical qubits encoded per physical data qubit. Recent quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) constructions have entered the ultra-high-rate regime with encoding rates above 1/2, but their syndrome-extraction circuits generally rely on reconfigurable connectivity or long-range qubit transport, making them difficult to implement on…

items.title: Collective coupling of over 100 individually trapped atoms to a single cavity mode
items.summary: Coupling optical tweezer arrays to high-finesse cavities provides a shared optical interface for neutral-atom registers. Scaling this interface to large tweezer arrays requires placing many traps within the coupling region of a single cavity mode while maintaining uniform trapping and site-resolved detection.

items.title: Phase-conjugate Gaussian encoding for continuous-variable quantum key distribution with a single phase-sensitive amplifier
items.summary: Phase-conjugate encoding is naturally compatible with shared phase-sensitive amplification and joint detection, offering a compact optical receiver architecture for continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD). Here, we develop a unified encoding and security framework for two-mode Gaussian CVQKD with tunable phase-conjugate intermode correlations matched to a joint receiver comprising a single phase-sensitive amplifier (PSA) and one balanced photodetector.

items.title: Lower bounds for testing the completely depolarizing channel
items.summary: We study lower bounds to the query complexity of testing whether an unknown quantum channel mapping a $d_{\mathrm{in}}$-dimensional input to a $d_{\mathrm{out}}$-dimensional output is the completely depolarizing channel or is $\varepsilon$-far from it in diamond distance. We show that for this task (i) any ancilla-assisted, coherent, adaptive tester requires at least $Ω(d_{\mathrm{in}}d_{\mathrm{out}}/\varepsilon^2)$ queries; (ii) any ancilla-assisted, coherent, non-adaptive tester requires at least…

items.title: Formally verified harness for Shor's order finding algorithm with $O(n^{2+ε})$ gate cost
items.summary: It is commonly understood that factoring a general $n$-bit biprime via Shor's order finding algorithm requires $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ gates by leveraging schoolbook integer arithmetics for addition and multiplication. Recent developments in quantum arithmetic circuits leveraging recursive Toom-Cook schemes have improved the cost scaling to $O(n^{2+ε})$.

items.title: Response-Threshold Framework for First-Peak Preservation in Noisy Grover Search
items.summary: Grover search is executed only after integer iterations, so noise can alter the stopping decision even when a continuous first peak remains visible. We develop a response-threshold framework separating continuous peak motion, stroboscopic geometry, and the discrete sampled-success argmax.

items.title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
items.summary: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity.

items.title: Pilot-waves and copilot-particles: A nonstochastic approach to objective wavefunction collapse
items.summary: We propose an extension to Schrödinger’s equation that incorporates macroscopic measurement-induced wavefunction collapse. We find that a hybrid between two leading approaches, the Bohm-de Broglie pilot-wave and objective collapse theories, accomplishes this goal in accordance with Born’s rule.

items.title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
items.summary: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field.

items.title: Chronic hydrocephalus after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a brain–CSF interface framework for mechanisms, conceptual states, and surgical management
items.summary: Chronic hydrocephalus following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) may be more usefully conceptualized as the cumulative failure of several interacting brain–CSF boundaries than as a single obstructed conduit. A purely mechanical model cannot account for inflammatory CSF secretion, delayed absorptive failure, impaired clearance, altered tissue compliance, or the heterogeneous need for permanent shunting, so we use a brain–CSF interface and compartment framework to organize these observations.

items.title: Exceptional structure and Lifshitz criticality in a non-Hermitian Kitaev chain
items.summary: We study an exactly solvable non-Hermitian $N$-site Kitaev chain with unequal pair-creation and pair-annihilation amplitudes and vanishing intersite hopping. We show that the chain supports an exceptional point (EP) at which all the many-body energies collapse to zero and the largest Jordan block grows quadratically with $N$.

items.title: Graph spectra and late-time concurrence in a lossy reservoir network
items.summary: We investigate how coupling the local environments of noninteracting qubits into a network changes their late-time entanglement dynamics. Each qubit interacts with a lossy bosonic memory mode, with coherent hopping between memory modes determined by an underlying graph.

items.title: Pre-amplification for Preserving Quantum Resources Through an Open-Air, Room-Temperature Microwave Channel
items.summary: We model a scenario where the pre-amplified signal mode of a two-mode squeezed vacuum (TMSV) state generated by a Josephson parametric converter (JPC) is transmitted through a room-temperature, open-air channel, while the idler is retained at low temperature. Before transmission, the state contains three quantum resources: (1) entanglement, (2) non-classicality, and (3) sub-vacuum conditional prediction of the signal quadrature.

items.title: feedback-grape: A JAX-based Python Package for GPU-Accelerated GRAPE with Feedback
items.summary: Modern quantum technology applications require accurate control of quantum systems, including a feedback loop in the control process. While open-loop control can be performed using well established gradient methods like GRadient Ascent Pulse Engineering (GRAPE), it was until recently unclear how to combine these with feedback from measurements, which are inherently non-differentiable.

items.title: Casimir-like wormholes
items.summary: We investigate spherically symmetric spacetimes sourced by matter with energy density $ρ\propto 1/r^{4}$ and equation of state $p_r = ωρ$. We derive the most general solution of Einstein's equations for this class of sources, obtaining black holes, naked singularities and traversable wormholes, parametrized by the integration constants and $ω$.

items.title: Mixed-state topological transitions with hidden long-range correlations
items.summary: We study a decoherence-driven transition from a one-dimensional symmetry-protected topological state to a trivial product state. The decoherence acts onsite while preserving the protecting symmetry on average.

items.title: Generative Models using Multi-layer Quantum Extreme Learning Machines
items.summary: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) and the closely related quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) paradigm exploit the complex dynamics of an uncontrolled quantum system for machine learning, offering an alternative to variational quantum algorithms whose training is hindered by barren plateaus and costly circuit optimization. Because the quantum system itself is left fixed, learning reduces to fitting a linear readout of a set of measured observables, and no gradient is ever taken through the quantum device.

items.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
items.summary: We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity.

items.title: A Forward Bit Makes Error Correction Dispensable for Antidegradable Amplitude-Damping Channels
items.summary: Preserving a qubit usually relies on redundant encoding over many uses of a noisy channel. We prove that for antidegradable amplitude damping, one channel use with one forward classical bit matches or beats every forward-assisted or unassisted code with any number of uses.

items.title: Readout errors limit how far adaptive quantum circuits can entangle
items.summary: Measurement and feedforward let quantum circuits entangle arbitrarily distant qubits in constant depth if measurement records are perfect and classical communication is instantaneous. We allow each reported bit to flip independently with a fixed probability between zero and one half, keeping all gates ideal.

items.title: Imperfect Cavities Select Better: Enantioselectivity Beyond Pure Helicity
items.summary: Single-handed light appears ideally suited to select a preferred handedness of matter. For chiral molecules in a cavity, we show that this intuition fails. Hybridization of light and matter reshapes the optical resonance through a self-energy that mixes opposite helicities.

items.title: Hardware-Aware Realization of Deterministic Quantum-Walk Search on Complete Bipartite Graphs
items.summary: Complete bipartite graphs offer a canonical platform for deterministic quantum search with quadratic speedup. We report the first experimental realization of deterministic discrete-time quantum-walk search over complete bipartite graphs, enabled by high-fidelity operations and a dynamical-phase compensation scheme, using a digital gate-based processor rather than an evolution-based platform.

items.title: Polarization waves in open-barrier quantum-dot cellular automata
items.summary: Quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) are almost always operated as bistable digital logic. We develop a closed-form theory of small-signal polarization waves in the open-barrier regime, where tunnelling within each cell is comparable to or stronger than the electrostatic kink coupling between cells, so that a line of cells responds linearly instead of latching.

items.title: Symmetric dilations of multi-qubit Pauli channels and semigroups
items.summary: We explore the symmetry properties of Stinespring dilations of single-qubit Pauli channels, addressing both the generic case and the specific examples of phase damping and depolarizing channels. For each scenario, we derive the representation of the Pauli group acting on the Hilbert space of the environment.

items.title: Observing Bell inequality violation beyond the qubit bound in a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate
items.summary: Correlations allowed by quantum mechanics can defy any classical explanation, with Bell nonlocality standing as their most profound and operationally powerful manifestation. While nonlocality has been demonstrated across a wide range of platforms, in many-body systems it has remained limited to ensembles of qubits, leaving the observation of higher-dimensional multipartite Bell correlations an open challenge.

items.title: The entangled loop: Emotion, interference and hierarchy in the architecture of consciousness
items.summary: Why does consciousness feel like something, and why is experience unified rather than fragmented? We propose that these properties arise from an entangled trefoil of emotion, interference-based inference and hierarchical orchestration, shaped by the thermodynamic constraint that living systems must remain far from equilibrium using limited energy.

items.title: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life
items.summary: Continual agents must handle urgent interaction while retaining alternatives, replaying errors, and committing safe long-term changes. A previous digital-life framework distinguishes online (busy) and offline (idle) channels, but leaves open whether these are separate programs or phases of a common process and how their operations should be ordered.

items.title: A systems-level energetic framework for conscious processing: energetic organization as a constraint on large-scale neural integration
items.summary: Conscious processing is associated with coordinated interactions among distributed neural systems, yet the biological constraints that enable and sustain large-scale neural integration remain incompletely understood. Contemporary theories emphasize computational, informational, and network mechanisms, while the potential contribution of systems-level energetic organization has received comparatively less explicit theoretical attention.

items.title: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice
items.summary: In the present paper we study the formulation of a search problem and the efficiency of multi-particle quantum walk search algorithms. The discrete-time evolution of each particle in space is treated according to Grover's quantum walk evolution operator.

items.title: Residual Entanglement vs. Residual Coherence: A Wave Packet Approach in Neutrino Oscillation with Matter
items.summary: In this work, we investigate quantum correlations in three-flavor neutrino oscillations beyond the standard plane-wave (PW) description by employing a wave-packet formalism in the presence of constant matter density. We study three quantum correlation measures, namely the residual $l_1$-norm coherence, Concurrence Fill, and Three-$π$ entanglement, and express them in terms of transition probabilities for an initial muon-flavor state.

items.title: Emergent Causality from Decoherence: A Postulated Regime with an Explicit Conjecture
items.summary: Emergent Causality from Decoherence: A Postulated Regime with an Explicit Conjecture An imaginary hypothesis, not a theory. This is the third revision. It corrects the definition of causality, changes the parameter, acknowledges the circularity of time, and states the conjecture explicitly.

items.title: Attention Renders Sensory Contents into Conscious State via Content-invariant Frontal-Posterior Coupling in Humans
items.summary: Abstract Although attention promotes conscious perception, how it does so remains unclear. Human neuroimaging research has richly characterized attentional modulation upon visual processing, yet it remains unclear which of its components act as precursors of consciousness, which constitute consciousness itself, and which merely reflect post-perceptual, response-related operations.

items.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
items.summary: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. In standard bedside assessments, these stimuli are applied manually, resulting in substantial variation in force, duration, frequency, and location.

items.title: Digital Minds: Issues in the Philosophy of Mind and Cognitive Science
items.summary: ABSTRACT This article provides a contemporary introduction to issues in the philosophy of mind and cognitive science that are studied within the emerging field of digital minds research. We explore the potential for AI systems to have mental states.

items.title: Local enhancement of finite-strength code preparation: recoverability and Wilson coherence
items.summary: Stabilizer measurements provide a direct route to preparing quantum error-correcting codes and long-range entangled states. In realistic implementations, however, finite measurement strength can coherently deform the encoding map away from the projective limit.

items.title: Probing chaos and criticality with observational entropy and finite-resolution measurements
items.summary: Coarse-grained measurements offer a scalable alternative to full state tomography for characterizing complex quantum dynamics. We show that observational entropy (OE), an information-theoretic entropy defined directly from finite-resolution measurement outcomes, provides a unified and experimentally accessible framework for quantifying chaos and probing criticality.

items.title: Quantum resources for everlasting communication security
items.summary: Abstract Quantum cryptography provides communication with everlasting security—a property unattainable by classical or post-quantum cryptography. Traditionally, quantum cryptography proclaims everlasting security by relying on principles such as no-cloning theorem, Bell inequalities, or the uncertainty principle, along with the standard assumption that legitimate users have no control over the communication channel.

items.title: The quantum-ready college: quantum technologies as an industry shift and how higher education should prepare
items.summary: Purpose This paper examines the emerging industry shift in which quantum technologies are evolving from isolated scientific breakthroughs into full-scale innovation ecosystems that will reshape higher education. Its purpose is to demonstrate why colleges must prepare now, well before fault tolerant quantum computers arrive, by developing quantum ready capacities across curriculum, workforce development, partnerships and cybersecurity.

items.title: Quantum Searching and Optimization Algorithms: A Comprehensive Guide
items.summary: This book offers a rigorous and forward-looking exploration of one of the most consequential frontiers in modern computation: the use of quantum mechanics to accelerate search, optimization, learning, simulation, and secure information processing. It begins by establishing the conceptual and mathematical foundations of quantum computation, including quantum gates, circuit design, quantum parallelism, and the distinctions between classical and quantum models of information processing.

items.title: Unitarity with respect to the clock of a dynamical local observer and the Einstein equivalence principle
items.summary: We investigate the unitarity of quantum evolution relative to an internal time defined by a local observer's clock. The observer is modeled as a relativistic particle carrying both a clock and a matter-field detector, analyzed first on a fixed curved background and subsequently within a fully diffeomorphism-invariant theory of dynamical gravity.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics of Local Anesthetics in Fascial Plane Blocks: Clinical Implications and Safety Considerations-A Narrative Review
items.summary: Fascial plane blocks (FPBs) are increasingly used in modern regional anaesthesia and differ from conventional nerve blocks by delivering local anesthetic (LA) into interfascial compartments. This approach results in distinct pharmacokinetics with clinically relevant systemic absorption.

items.summary: General anesthetics like sevoflurane are clinically essential, yet the neural circuits governing their induction of unconsciousness and recovery remain incompletely defined. Here, we show the potential involvement of the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (Vglut2)-expressing glutamatergic neurons in the central medial thalamus (CMT Vglut2 neurons) in modulation states of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia.

items.title: From unimodal to multimodal deep physiological signal analysis in healthcare: A survey of models, fusion and explainability
items.summary: Physiological signal analysis supports objective assessment of emotion, stress, pain, and disease progression in healthcare systems. Early research focused mainly on unimodal signals, which perform well in controlled settings but are often affected by noise, limited contextual information and reduced generalisability.

items.title: Patient-specific factors are associated with distinct brain network connectivity in disorders of consciousness
items.summary: Disorders of consciousness (DoC) arise from diverse etiologies and exhibit substantial clinical heterogeneity, including variations in patient age and time since injury.
